subject: Acme POC: success criteria & provisioning next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Acme POC: success criteria & provisioning next steps

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before we kick off the POC: 

High-level goal
- Validate Redwood’s inference runtime on your primary document-summary pipeline (avg doc length ~1k tokens) and measure latency/cost at 99th pct throughput.

Success criteria (what Acme will consider a successful POC)
- 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for single-request summaries at our target batch sizes
- End-to-end cost per 1k tokens at or below $X (we’ll run calibrated workload)
- No functional regressions on summary quality vs your baseline (BLEU/ROUGE checks and 10 critical prompts)
- Smooth integration with your Okta SSO and approval for production API key issuance if satisfied

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Provision access (API key, IP allowlist, SSO invites), share POC checklist
- Week 1: Ingest sample dataset + run baseline tests (we’ll provide scripts)
- Week 2: Performance tuning + joint review; pass/fail decision at end of Week 2

Owners
- Redwood: Marissa (overall program owner), Dylan (technical lead — runtime/config), Neha (security/compliance contact)
- Acme: Ethan (technical lead), Priya (procurement/legal)

Immediate asks from Acme to enable provisioning
1) Okta metadata or SAML SP details (entityID, ACS URL) for SSO invite
2) IP ranges to allowlist (CIDR blocks) for the POC API key
3) List of users to invite to SSO (name + email)

Attachments: I’ve attached the POC_Checklist.xlsx — it includes the test plan and scripts we’ll run.

Next steps
- If you can send the Okta metadata + IP ranges today, we’ll queue the SSO invites and issue a scoped API key (read-only + inference) by tomorrow EOD.
- I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff once access is provisioned.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0187

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC: success criteria & provisioning next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. TL;DR — we can provision as requested; I’ll own the technical pieces. Plan:

1) Create a scoped API key for Acme (restricted to inference endpoints, token limits per-minute).
2) Add the provided IP CIDRs to our allowlist for that key.
3) Send Okta SSO invites (we use SAML; will need SP metadata).
4) Open a support ticket for audit logs retention policy for the POC (Neha, can you confirm retention default and if Acme needs anything special?)

Marissa — can you confirm the exact list of users for SSO invites? We usually send invites from identity@redwood.com; if Acme prefers leaning on Just-In-Time provisioning instead, let us know.

I’ll target issuing the API key and SSO invites by Fri EOD once we have metadata + IP ranges. I’ll also attach the onboarding snippet and our SSO config guide in the ticket.

—
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.com
